name: HP INC.
moat_justification: Weak-to-moderate moat: scale as the #2 global PC vendor and the #1 print vendor with a high-margin supplies annuity and commercial channel/service relationships, but PC hardware is commoditized (no OS or chip control, thin Personal Systems margins), switching costs are low outside managed commercial fleets, and printing is in secular decline against Lenovo/Dell/Apple competition and digitization.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 11 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.2%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Mature cash generator, moat 4/10 — on a TTM base it comes close but does not clear 15% (13.95% weighted IRR, IV@15% $27.71 vs $30.23 price); it clears 15% at or below $27.71.
moat_for: #2 global PC vendor at scale — global distribution and channel strength
#1 in print with a high-margin supplies/cartridge annuity on the installed base
Commercial fleet and managed-print relationships with service attach
Printing operating margin far above Personal Systems (18.1% vs 4.6% in Q3 FY26)
moat_against: PC hardware commoditized — no OS/chip control, thin Personal Systems margins
Printing in secular decline — revenue, supplies and hardware units all fell in Q3 FY26
Low switching costs outside managed commercial fleets; Lenovo, Dell and Apple compete on price and premium
Memory/component cost inflation and tariff exposure squeeze gross margin
Recent growth is ASP/pull-forward driven while unit shipments fall sharply
